title: Vanished Trades
desc: A grades 5-8 investigation about jobs the modern world left behind: identify each trade, what the worker did, and what replaced the job.
teks: Social Studies (19 TAC Ch. 113) + Career Development (Ch. 127)
themeNote: Occupations are examined as evidence of how technology and the economy change the world of work; dates are approximate.

ui.welcome.title: Vanished Trades
ui.welcome.subtitle: Can you name the jobs the modern world left behind?
ui.welcome.body: Work changes with technology. Whole jobs that once filled the streets have simply disappeared. Step into the record of vanished trades to investigate nine jobs from the past: name each one, learn what the worker did, and discover what replaced them.
ui.directions.title: How to investigate each trade
ui.directions.body1: Study the image and clues. First, identify the vanished trade. Next, decide what the worker actually did. Finally, choose what replaced the job.
ui.directions.body2: You may revisit exhibits before submitting your final answers.
ui.directions.step1body: Use the clues to name the vanished trade.

ui.list.body: Each desk opens a three-part investigation. Finished exhibits stay available for review.

exhibits.limitation: Electric lights could be switched on all at once, with no worker needed
clues: Each evening I walked the streets with a long pole.
I lit the gas lamps that lined the roads.
At dawn I returned to put the flames out.
My job vanished when a switch could light a whole street.

purpose: Lit and put out the gas street lamps each day

exhibits.purpose: Lit and put out the gas street lamps each day

exhibits.limitation: Automatic switching let callers dial each other directly
clues: I sat before a wall of wires and plugs.
I connected one caller to another by hand.
Callers reached me before they could reach anyone else.
I often knew everyone's business in a small town.

purpose: Connected telephone calls by plugging wires into a switchboard

exhibits.purpose: Connected telephone calls by plugging wires into a switchboard

exhibits.limitation: Electric refrigerators made cold at home, so no ice was needed
clues: I carried heavy blocks with large metal tongs.
I delivered to a wooden box that kept food cold.
Families put a card in the window to show how much they needed.
My job melted away when a machine could make cold at home.

purpose: Delivered blocks of ice to keep food cold in an icebox

exhibits.purpose: Delivered blocks of ice to keep food cold in an icebox

exhibits.limitation: Newspapers and radio could reach far more people at once
clues: I rang a bell and shouted 'Hear ye! Hear ye!'
I read news and orders aloud in the town square.
Most people could not read, so they listened to me.
Printed news and radio replaced my booming voice.

purpose: Announced news, laws, and events aloud to the public

exhibits.purpose: Announced news, laws, and events aloud to the public

exhibits.limitation: Cheap alarm clocks let people wake themselves
clues: Before alarm clocks, families paid me to wake them.
I tapped on bedroom windows with a long stick.
Some of us used a pea-shooter to reach high windows.
A cheap alarm clock finally put me out of work.

purpose: Woke workers on time by tapping on their windows

exhibits.purpose: Woke workers on time by tapping on their windows

exhibits.limitation: Cheap factory-made metal and plastic containers took over
clues: I shaped wooden staves and bound them with metal hoops.
I made barrels, buckets, and casks.
Almost everything was once shipped and stored in my barrels.
Factory-made containers replaced my craft.

purpose: Made wooden barrels and casks to store and ship goods
Forged tools and horseshoes from iron
Shaped bowls and jars from clay

exhibits.purpose: Made wooden barrels and casks to store and ship goods

exhibits.limitation: Automatic push-button elevators let riders run them alone
clues: I rode up and down inside a lift all day.
I pulled a lever to stop level with each floor.
I called out the floors and the shops on them.
Push-button elevators finally made me unnecessary.

purpose: Operated a manual elevator and stopped it level with each floor
Carried guests' luggage in a hotel
Opened the door for building visitors

exhibits.purpose: Operated a manual elevator and stopped it level with each floor

exhibits.limitation: Electronic computers calculated far faster and without tiring
clues: Long ago, 'computer' was a job title for a person.
I solved long math problems by hand, all day.
Teams of us worked out tables, orbits, and trajectories.
Electronic machines took my name and my job.

purpose: Worked out long calculations by hand, often in large teams

exhibits.purpose: Worked out long calculations by hand, often in large teams

exhibits.limitation: Automatic pinsetting machines did the job faster and cheaper
clues: At the bowling alley, I sat above the lanes.
I cleared the fallen pins and set them up again.
I jumped down to send the ball back to the bowlers.
A machine now does my job at the end of every lane.

purpose: Reset the pins and returned balls by hand at a bowling alley
Showed people to their theater seats
Mixed sodas at a fountain counter

exhibits.purpose: Reset the pins and returned balls by hand at a bowling alley

correlation.expectation: Students explain how technological change affects the goods and services produced and the jobs available.
correlation.alignment: Each exhibit ties a vanished job to the technology that replaced it.

correlation.expectation: Students analyze how scientific and technological changes affect the way people live and work.
correlation.alignment: Nine trades show cause-and-effect between invention and the disappearance of work.

correlation.expectation: Students investigate how careers change over time and why some occupations decline.
correlation.alignment: Students reason about why each occupation faded and reflect on jobs that may change next.

correlation.expectation: Students sequence and describe changes across time periods.
correlation.alignment: Each reveal gives the era a trade was common and what came after.
